links.outcome: Differences between AI-generated contours and clinician-reviewed final contours, geometric and dosimetric
links.effect: Dosimetric comparison of AI-contours versus final reviewed contours showed clinically significant dose differences for larynx and elective nodal volumes, so clinician review altered contours; authors conclude final clinician review remains essential.
links.quote: Dosimetric evaluation demonstrated clinically significant dose differences for larynx and elective nodal volumes.

links.outcome: Retrospective local comparison of AI contours to clinically used contours (VDSC, blinded preference)
links.effect: Median VDSC varied widely by structure (0.23-0.88); blinded preference was 31.4% clinician, 32.9% AI, 35.7% no difference, revealing local protocol differences.
links.quote: Retrospective median VDSC varied widely for different structures (0.23-0.88).

screen.reason: Evaluates commercial AI autocontouring software prospectively in a real-world clinical workflow, assessing time savings, qualitative usability, and the impact/necessity of clinician review and editing (human-in-the-loop).

primary.practice: clinician review and editing of AI contours
